verdict.rationale: PayPal's ACP path documents a delegated Braintree token that is single-use, bound to a merchant ID, and carries configurable amount and time restrictions, so all three scope dimensions exist. The UCP path also returns a Braintree single-use token. However, the docs are written for merchants consuming the token. They do not show an end user creating or configuring a scoped credential to hand to their own agent. Missing for 10: user-facing controls to issue and configure limits, multi-use or limited-use credentials beyond one-time tokens, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand my agent a scoped, limited-use payment credential — amount limits, expiry, merchant restrictions — instead of a raw card number

citations.quote: bound to your merchant ID and includes amount and time restrictions that you can configure.
is a one-time-use token that you can process using your existing Braintree integration
the payment payload includes the Braintree single-use token in the `credential.token` field
